exposure: Obstetric variables (nulliparity, cephalic presentation, singleton pregnancy, term gestation)
outcome: Exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) rates at hospital discharge
cohort: The study included 23,037 births, classified using the Robson Ten-Group Classification System, that occurred at Hospital Universitario de la Ribera in Spain between 2010 and 2023.
finding: The study found an overall exclusive breastfeeding rate of 74.10% at hospital discharge, with significant variation across Robson groups, where Group 1 showed the highest rate (78.339%) and Group 8 had the lowest (56.485%).
mod_finding: The study found significant variation in EBF rates across Robson groups, which classify births based on obstetric characteristics influencing mode of birth, where Group 1 (typically low-risk for caesarean section) demonstrated the highest EBF rates, while Groups 8 (all multiple pregnancies), 5 (multiparous, previous CS), and 7 (multiparous, singleton, breech) exhibited the lowest.
